from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Bridge from Geometry to Abstraction", [
            "Vectors are more than just arrows in space.",
            "We focus on behavior and interaction rules.",

        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Simple arrow
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(Indicate(arrow, color=YELLOW))

        blob = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#00BFFF", fill_opacity=0.5)

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Eight Axioms: The Rules of the Game", [
            "Vector spaces rely on eight specific axioms.",
            "These define addition and scalar multiplication rules.",
            "They ensure consistency across different systems.",
            "Everything must satisfy closure and identity.",
            "Inverse and distributive laws are also required."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        axioms = VGroup(*[Text(f"Axiom {i+1}", font_size=20) for i in range(8)])
        for i, ax in enumerate(axioms):
            self.place_at_grid(ax, f"{chr(65 + i // 3)}{1 + (i % 3)}", scale_factor=0.8)
            
        add_label = Text("Addition", color=WHITE)
        scalar_label = Text("Scalar Mult", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(add_label, "E1", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(scalar_label, "E4", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        checkmark = Star(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axioms))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(add_label.animate.set_color("#32CD32"), scalar_label.animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Flash(checkmark, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        closure_txt = Text("Closure & Identity", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(closure_txt, "F1", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(closure_txt), closure_txt.animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFA500")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        inverse_dist_txt = Text("Inverse & Distributive", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(inverse_dist_txt, "F4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(inverse_dist_txt), inverse_dist_txt.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Vector spaces are defined by their structure.",
            "They serve as foundations for modern science.",
            "Abstraction empowers us to solve complex problems."
        ])
        
        # Create visual elements
        vs_structure = Text("Vector Space Structure", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        modern_science = Text("Modern Science", font_size=30, color="#32CD32")
        complexity_solved = Text("Complexity Solved", font_size=30, color="#32CD32")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the text 'Vector Space Structure'. Color: #FFFFFF.
        self.place_at_grid(vs_structure, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(vs_structure))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Expand the text to fill the screen, showing it as a foundation. Color: #87CEEB.
        self.play(
            vs_structure.animate.scale(1.5).set_color("#87CEEB"),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in 'Modern Science' and 'Complexity Solved' bullet points. Color: #32CD32.
        self.place_at_grid(modern_science, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(complexity_solved, 'E5')
        self.play(
            FadeIn(modern_science),
            FadeIn(complexity_solved),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32")
        )
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Bridge from Geometry to Abstraction
sections.content: Review the familiar 2D/3D vectors (arrows). Introduce the paradigm shift: Instead of focusing on 'arrows,' we focus on the 'behavior' (the rules of addition and scaling).
sections.example: Visual: An arrow in 2D space morphing into a abstract 'cloud' of points to represent that the nature of the object doesn't matter, only how it interacts.

sections.title: The Eight Axioms: The Rules of the Game
sections.content: Define a Vector Space as a set with two operations (Addition and Scalar Multiplication) satisfying 8 axioms (Closure, Associativity, Commutativity, Identity, Inverse, Distributivity, etc.).
sections.example: Visual: A 'Rulebook' animation where 8 icons represent axioms. If an object 'obeys' all 8, it earns the title 'Vector'.

sections.title: Beyond Arrows: Unexpected Spaces
sections.content: Demonstrate that 'vectors' can be functions, matrices, or sequences. This expands the students' mental model beyond physical geometry.
sections.example: Visual: A split-screen showing a 3D arrow, a 2x2 matrix, and a polynomial f(x) = ax² + bx + c. The narrator shows that adding two polynomials follows the same 'rules' as adding two arrows.

sections.title: Applied Logic: The 'Animal Weight' Problem
sections.content: Introduce a scenario to test if a set forms a vector space. If we define a set of 'animals' where we can 'scale' their size and 'add' their attributes, does it satisfy the zero-vector and inverse axioms?
sections.example: Visual: A funny animation of a cat scaled by 2 (2x cat) vs. a 'negative' cat (the inverse). We quickly see that biological animals usually fail the 'inverse' axiom, proving they don't form a vector space.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap that a Vector Space is a structure defined by its properties, not its appearance. This is the foundation for Linear Algebra, Quantum Mechanics, and Data Science.
sections.example: Visual: A 'Toolbox' icon labeled 'Vector Space' containing symbols for sounds, images, and numbers, reinforcing that abstraction is a tool for problem-solving.
